about: Takrar's own list (own work). Only occasions tied to a cited act of worship; observances whose religious status is disputed are left out. Dates are worked out from the Hijri calendar and shown as expected. 'citation' is a hadith lead and stays empty until its collection and number are confirmed in two witnesses (spec 5.1); 'quran' is a Quran reference rendered from the bundled surah files.

events.title: Ramadan
events.description: The month of fasting, from Fajr to Maghrib each day.

events.title: The last ten nights
events.description: The closing nights of Ramadan, when Laylat al-Qadr is sought. Each night begins at the Maghrib before its date.

events.title: Eid al-Fitr
events.description: The Eid that closes Ramadan, with the Eid prayer in the morning.

events.title: Six days of Shawwal
events.description: Six voluntary fasts in Shawwal, after Eid day.

events.title: First ten days of Dhul-Hijjah
events.description: Days in which good deeds are especially encouraged, ending with Eid al-Adha.

events.title: Day of Arafah
events.description: The day pilgrims stand at Arafah. Those not on Hajj may keep a voluntary fast.

events.title: Eid al-Adha
events.description: The Eid of sacrifice, with the Eid prayer in the morning.

events.title: Days of tashriq
events.description: The three days after Eid al-Adha, days of eating, drinking and remembering Allah.

events.title: Tasu'a
events.description: The ninth of Muharram, a voluntary fast kept together with Ashura.

events.title: Ashura
events.description: The tenth of Muharram, a voluntary fast.

events.title: The white days
events.description: Voluntary fasts on the 13th, 14th and 15th of the Hijri month.
